    A compact bilateral filter keeps the core NumPy-only.  The range scale is
    estimated from the image itself, so it smooths TEM/SEM shot noise without
    averaging a bright particle edge into its background.

DNA Moiré Designer prototype

This project uses the calibrated S8-R4x4C Square-Square bilayer model.

Return perfect-duplex DNA Tm in Celsius using nearest neighbors.

    ``strand_nm`` and ``target_nm`` are the concentrations of the two
    distinct, non-self-complementary strands.  Mg is converted to a sodium
    equivalent and the SantaLucia entropy salt correction is then applied.

Return clipped helix centres and nearest-neighbour lattice bonds.

    ``lattice_constant_nm`` is the Square nearest-neighbour spacing and the
    Kagome triangular Bravais constant used by the prediction model.  Kagome
    nearest neighbours are therefore separated by half that value.

Deterministic staged structure generation for the Square moire seed.

The public functions in this module deliberately keep caDNAno model imports
out of the GUI process.  The model worker runs in a short-lived subprocess,
then this module validates the legacy JSON before the UI exposes it.

Infer rendered-image signal direction without assuming modality.

    A representative particle is strongest evidence.  Otherwise compare the
    robust positive and negative detail tails after local-background removal.
    This intentionally describes image signal, not AFM physical height.

Central, offline localization for the Moiré Designer UI and exports.

The application historically contained literal Chinese/English UI strings.
This module deliberately translates at the presentation boundary so existing
design algorithms and serialized scientific identifiers stay unchanged.

Run the existing orthogonal-sequence designer inside DNA Moiré Designer.

The parameter dialog and generation/export flow intentionally mirror the
existing implementation.  This module owns the launch path so opening the
tool never requires a cadnano document controller or cadnano main window.
zh_CN.Use one arithmetic-mean frame size per r:
Use one arithmetic-mean frame size per reference role and shape.

    Each exemplar keeps its own image texture and angle.  Only the search-frame
    width/height are standardized, so a slightly loose or tight automatic fit
    does not propagate as a separate particle size throughout the image.

Export a template, enter the sequences, and import it; template controls appear below the detected results on the right. For identical layers, enter each sequence once and copy it to the corresponding position.
zh_CN.Build a calibrated prediction for the se:
Build a calibrated prediction for the selected bilayer and Square Seed.

    Nominal Z lengths remain independent design inputs.  Angle/period solves
    the distributed mean indel, which changes the mean physical Z2/spacing
    length while leaving its shared SST/Seed crossover coordinates intact.
zh_CN.Generate a diverse orthogonal set using:
Generate a diverse orthogonal set using bounded pool-based selection.

    The best candidate from a small valid pool is selected at every step,
    rather than permanently accepting the first random hit.  This retains the
    simplicity of rejection sampling while reducing order-dependent collapse.
zh_CN.Close one measured open seam along both:
Close one measured open seam along both possible frame routes.

    This makes the numerical area and translucent overlay use the same
    precise TEM-refined boundary, rather than the earlier local-FFT cell
    staircase.  More complex multi-domain topologies retain the conservative
    cell-based fallback.
zh_CN.Use one color for both 16-bp halves of e:
Use one color for both 16-bp halves of every 32-bp pair.

    Physical A0/B0 staples and the normal staples occupying the legal A1/B1
    extension targets use the same pair color.  Thus each layer has one color
    per 32-bp capture pair even before translated capture sequences are
    materialized during export.
zh_CN.1. Upload a TEM image; its name may begi:
1. Upload a TEM image; its name may begin with '<value> <unit>_' (for example, 20 nm_xx)
2. Select single-layer or bilayer analysis
3. Click Analyze to detect the scale bar and analyze the TEM image and FFT automatically
4. Verify the scale and results; enter the scale manually only when OCR and the file name provide no scale
zh_CN.Locate repeated TEM units near an FFT-pr:
Locate repeated TEM units near an FFT-predicted period.

    A normalized template correlation supplies candidate unit centres. The
    final period is the median of neighbour distances along two approximately
    orthogonal axes, so the FFT prediction constrains the search without
    forcing the TEM measurement to equal it.
zh_CN.Return complete 16-bp domain bounds arou:
Return complete 16-bp domain bounds around each duplex layer.

    The five validated 96/104/112/120/128-bp examples alternate which
    polymer owns the eight-base outer overhang.  Repeating that boundary
    state every 32 bp makes lengthening the exact inverse of shortening:
    only complete 32-nt U strands are added or removed.
zh_CN.Methods mixed into ``MoireDesignerWindow:
Methods mixed into ``MoireDesignerWindow``.

    All raster exports use the exact TEM source width and height and SVG view
    boxes use those same dimensions.  Embedded FFTs additionally use isotropic
    reciprocal-space axes, so a rectangular TEM cannot stretch FFT angles or
    turn a Square first-order peak set into a rectangle.
zh_CN.Estimate the short lattice spacing direc:
Estimate the short lattice spacing directly from TEM autocorrelation.

    This is deliberately independent of the reciprocal-space distance used
    for the FFT value reported in the bulk CSV.  The FFT estimate is only used
    to define a broad, physically plausible annulus; the final distance comes
    from real-space correlation peaks.
zh_CN.Nick target-bearing staples at legal lon:
Nick target-bearing staples at legal longitudinal positions.

    A connected physical staple already includes its 16-nt capture segment,
    so 64 nt is an absolute limit and 57 nt is preferred.  A normal staple
    on a translated/export-only target must leave room for that future
    segment: its corresponding limits are therefore 48 and 41 nt.
zh_CN.Straighten an isolated short product int:
Straighten an isolated short product into adjacent normal staples.

    This is the final edge-case repair for variable 8-bp endpoints.  It acts
    only on a non-capture component: internal crossovers of that short product
    are opened, each contiguous helix run is joined to a neighboring normal
    staple, and no Seed–SST edge is ever changed.
zh_CN.Seal boundary nicks until every non-capt:
Seal boundary nicks until every non-capture staple is synthesizable.

    Reference capture windows and automatically generated Seed routing meet
    at deterministic same-helix boundaries.  Sealing only an adjacent pair of
    open 5'/3' records preserves all crossover sites while avoiding small
    products caused solely by the former window crop.
zh_CN.Rotate a lattice graph and remove the co:
Rotate a lattice graph and remove the complete central Seed footprint.

    The exclusion square stays aligned with the Square Seed, matching the 2-D
    preview where both SST layers are drawn first and the full 8 x 8 Seed area
    is then cleared.  Edges touching a removed helix are removed as well, so
    no SST bond enters the reserved Seed area.
zh_CN.Build two permanent left/right Seed scaf:
Build two permanent left/right Seed scaffold molecules.

    This is deliberately a Moiré-only generator.  It reuses the validated
    Seed-S topology, preserves the balanced 10/11-bp outer edge adjustment,
    and joins complete secondary 32-bp modules with explicit seams.  It does
    not alter or configure cadnano's normal AutoCS_scaffolds command.
zh_CN.Return SST, Seed-support and maximum-den:
Return SST, Seed-support and maximum-density capture ranges.

    ``z1_bp``/``z3_bp`` remain the SST lengths for compatibility with staged
    files.  Seed targets are separate, single-base inputs.  Full coverage
    reserves three bases here; legal per-helix crossover endpoints and seams
    are realized by the routing worker without global 8-bp snapping.
zh_CN.Detect visible reciprocal peaks and pres:
Detect visible reciprocal peaks and preserve their complex phase.

    The detector uses the real FFT of the uploaded TEM, sub-pixel peak
    centroids, compact locally fitted ellipses, and exact Friedel partners.
    Raw arrays keep the source width:height ratio.  The GUI displays them on
    isotropic reciprocal-space axes, so FFT geometry is not stretched.
zh_CN.Remove only crossover blocks required to:
Remove only crossover blocks required to reunite dense loops.

    Adding all 1/32 candidates creates several legal closed loops.  Restoring
    a longitudinal block whose two crossover halves lie in different loops
    merges exactly those loops.  Repeating this operation produces one loop
    while retaining the maximum possible number of dense legal crossovers.
zh_CN.Extend only near-frame open endpoints to:
Extend only near-frame open endpoints to the image boundary.

    Local FFT windows cannot be centred closer than half a patch to an image
    edge.  Consequently, a real domain seam that exits the image is otherwise
    drawn with two short missing end pieces.  This function adds those pieces
    before TEM evidence refinement.  Closed/internal contours are untouched.
zh_CN.Return the Seed support target passed to:
Return the Seed support target passed to legal crossover routing.

    Seed input is intentionally single-base.  Endpoint legality is handled by
    the per-helix 10/11-bp edge redistribution and seam merger in the routing
    worker, so this stage must not round the whole support zone to 8 bp.
    Requested full coverage still reserves at least three bases beyond SST.
zh_CN.Translate a validated left/right routing:
Translate a validated left/right routing into balanced band bounds.

    Internal reciprocal crossover blocks keep their reference topology.
    The low edge is used as the translation anchor.  Endpoint crossovers are
    moved to the requested legal outer boundary, while crossover blocks that
    fall outside a shortened band are healed into ordinary longitudinal DNA.
zh_CN.Find an optional pore/supercell lattice:
Find an optional pore/supercell lattice sharing the helix orientation.

    A valid pore lattice must provide Friedel pairs along both axes of the
    already established single-layer Square helix lattice.  Its spacing must
    be a near-integer multiple of the helix spacing; this rejects arbitrary
    low-frequency texture, contamination and unrelated domain envelopes.

zh_CN.Resolve the two first-order Square Bragg:
Resolve the two first-order Square Bragg families from a TEM image.

    Median/mean patch spectra suppress the specimen envelope and the much
    lower-frequency moire modulation.  The closest-to-centre rule is applied
    only after sharp peaks have formed two reciprocal, orthogonal Square
    families; central background and moire satellites are therefore not
    eligible lattice peaks.
zh_CN.Frozen Square missing-helix calibration:
Frozen Square missing-helix calibration used by design prediction.

The nodes are the finalized 2026-08-02 SNUPI matrix.  Each profile is
``(x0, T0, k_minus, k_plus)`` and each descriptor contains missing fraction,
eccentricity, polar-moment ratio, boundary fraction, mean neighbour degree
and mean wall depth.  This copy keeps DNA Moiré Designer independent from a
particular cadnano installation.
zh_CN.Combine specimen contrast with the prove:
Combine specimen contrast with the proven domain-seam evidence.

    Sample/background classification and domain classification remain
    independent.  Only the final sub-pixel/vector placement is shared: broad
    mass-thickness contrast keeps the path on the specimen rim, while the
    texture-orientation and dark-ridge terms make it hug the visible TEM edge
    as accurately as a domain/domain boundary.
zh_CN.Return a symmetric, non-additive priorit:
Return a symmetric, non-additive priority for both pairwise risks.

    The same-substring and cross-complement objectives remain independent:
    first minimize whichever objective is closest to its own hard threshold,
    then minimize the other one.  Raw worst-case lengths break utilization
    ties.  Consequently, an excellent value in one objective can never
    compensate for a near-threshold value in the other.
zh_CN.Build an in-memory A1/B1 alternative use:
Build an in-memory A1/B1 alternative used only for sequence export.

    The accepted design remains A0/B0 and therefore connects only Seed
    helices 16–19 and 47–44 in public SST-first numbering.  This derived copy
    swaps those bridges for their 4x4-unit translations, allowing cadnano's
    sequence engine to calculate the other four helices on each face without
    adding those bridges to the accepted structure JSON.
zh_CN.Build one legal closed Seed band from tr:
Build one legal closed Seed band from translated native endpoints.

    Square scaffold endpoint phases repeat every 32 bases.  The validated
    Seed-S reference supplies complementary low/high endpoint matchings; a
    whole-period translation therefore remains a native crossover.  Keeping
    only those endpoint rings and then adding legal seams avoids translating
    hundreds of interior crossovers by helix-specific offsets.
zh_CN.Return real-space evidence specialized f:
Return real-space evidence specialized for specimen/background edges.

    Domain seams are dominated by lattice-orientation changes, whereas a
    specimen outline is usually expressed by a broad mass-thickness/tone edge
    plus a change in periodic texture.  Keeping these evidence maps separate
    prevents the sample contour from snapping to a strong internal lattice
    transition, as happened in high-resolution cryo/TEM fields.
zh_CN.Trace a mostly vertical/horizontal seam:
Trace a mostly vertical/horizontal seam at near-pixel resolution.

    A coarse local-FFT boundary is a staircase of cell edges.  Offsetting
    nodes only along each edge normal cannot turn that staircase into the
    oblique physical seam.  When the observed boundary is predominantly
    monotone, use every TEM row (or column) as a free path state and solve a
    continuity-regularized dynamic program through the dark-seam evidence.
zh_CN.Return multi-scale TEM evidence for a vi:
Return multi-scale TEM evidence for a visible grain/domain boundary.

    Local FFT determines which lattice family lies on each side.  The visible
    seam itself is positioned from the TEM: slow intensity edges, changes in
    local texture orientation/anisotropy, variance transitions and dark grain
    boundary ridges.  The calculation is deliberately performed at a bounded
    resolution and never invents a spline-smoothed boundary.
zh_CN.Remove local-FFT grid staircases while r:
Remove local-FFT grid staircases while retaining measured bends.

    TEM domain contours arrive as connected vector segments.  Douglas-Peucker
    reduction is applied independently to each open chain, followed by two
    conservative corner-cut passes.  The tolerance is tied to the local-FFT
    stride/search scale, so a visible large bend survives while dozens of
    horizontal/vertical micro-steps become one oblique or gently curved run.
zh_CN.Absolute lattice orientations for a TEM-:
Absolute lattice orientations for a TEM-registered reconstruction.

        FFT orientations are mathematical angles (positive y points upward).
        The returned values retain that convention; drawing code converts them
        to image coordinates.  When TEM real-space period supplies a refined
        relative twist, preserve the FFT-measured absolute mean orientation and
        distribute that refined twist symmetrically around the mean.
zh_CN.Absorb sub-32-bp crop remnants without d:
Absorb sub-32-bp crop remnants without deleting scaffold bases.

    Moving an old closure inward can leave a 20-bp terminal loop bounded by
    the old reciprocal crossover block.  It is not a complete 32-bp module
    and therefore must not receive a seam.  Removing that one crossover block
    restores both longitudinal bonds and absorbs the bases into the adjacent
    main loop.  Complete 32/64-bp modules are intentionally left for the
    explicit seam merger below.
zh_CN.Return geometry and text scales for anno:
Return geometry and text scales for annotations on Uploaded TEM.

        Geometry remains resolution-aware so boxes, markers and line weights
        keep their relative placement on the exported original-resolution
        image.  Font point sizes deliberately do *not* scale with raster pixel
        count: a cryo/high-resolution upload must use the same annotation type
        size as an ordinary TEM rather than treating extra pixels as a reason
        to enlarge its text.
zh_CN.Return TEM evidence centred on a visibly:
Return TEM evidence centred on a visibly dark twin/grain seam.

    An orientation-gradient map has two maxima, one on either shoulder of a
    dark physical seam.  Snapping to that map alone can therefore draw a line
    parallel to, but several pixels away from, the boundary.  For same-a,
    same-symmetry twins we combine the texture evidence with a dark
    difference-of-Gaussians ridge so the reported vector follows the seam
    centre rather than a local-FFT cell centre or one of its shoulders.
zh_CN.Map validated lattice families to their:
Map validated lattice families to their real-space domains.

    The historical name is retained for compatibility.  A family may contain
    the two reciprocal axes of a Square lattice or the three reciprocal axes
    of a sixfold lattice.  Global FFT establishes the allowed bases;
    overlapping local FFTs then assign symmetry, spacing and orientation to
    each spatial domain.  Connected components and boundaries are emitted in
    source-image coordinates for identical raster/SVG rendering by the GUI.
zh_CN.Return clear peaks belonging to validate:
Return clear peaks belonging to validated reciprocal bases.

    Every accepted Friedel pair must be expressible as

        G(h,k) = h*g1 + k*g2,  h,k integers.

    For Square this includes the familiar 45-degree (h,h)/(h,-h) diagonal
    shell.  Honeycomb/Kagome/hexagonal families use their measured oblique
    reciprocal basis, so their legal higher-order angles emerge from integer
    indices rather than from a hard-coded 45-degree rule.  Missing or weak
    theoretical reflections are never synthesized.

zh_CN.Build Square and sixfold lattice hypothe:
Build Square and sixfold lattice hypotheses from measured FFT peaks.

    Each hypothesis is an actual Friedel-paired set of reciprocal peaks.  The
    local-domain stage decides where it is present; no symmetry is inferred
    from a single line or from an unpaired maximum.  Honeycomb is reserved for
    a near-60/60/60 first-order family.  The user-supplied cryo-EM Kagome
    reference is represented by the experimentally distorted sixfold family,
    typically containing one 65--70 degree reciprocal-axis gap.  Ambiguous
    sixfold families remain explicitly ``Hexagonal``.
zh_CN.<b>These parameters can usually remain a:
These parameters can usually remain at their defaults.
• Classification backend: Built-in mode requires no external software; EMAN2 is available only when installed.
• Signal polarity, threshold, background flattening, and denoising strength are adjusted directly on the main page.
• Automatic group count: 0 uses the software recommendation; another value forces that number of groups.
• Template-matching threshold: higher values are stricter and reduce false positives; lower values increase recall.
• Density definition: material area uses the actual mask; outer-envelope area fills internal holes.
zh_CN.Fit an FFT without distorting reciprocal:
Fit an FFT without distorting reciprocal-space geometry.

        A rectangular TEM produces a rectangular FFT array, but one FFT pixel
        represents ``1 / image_width`` in x and ``1 / image_height`` in y.
        Treating those array pixels as equal-sized display pixels therefore
        stretches angles and a Square reciprocal lattice.  Fit by the
        *normalised frequency span* instead: the complete FFT is square and a
        fractional centre crop keeps the same physical x/y scale.  This is the
        native, undistorted reciprocal-space aspect used by the on-screen
        preview and by both PNG and SVG exports.
zh_CN.Materialize both 4x4 SST translations ar:
Materialize both 4x4 SST translations around the accepted 8x8 Seed.

    The accepted cadnano file intentionally contains only the origin A0/B0
    capture bridges.  Sequence export derives the A1/B1 translation in
    memory.  For the assembled atomistic model we need both physical copies:
    retain the accepted SST unit, duplicate the translated unit four lattice
    columns to its right, and apply the translated capture routing only to
    the second four helices on each Seed face.  The two face groups are
    disjoint, so this preserves the origin capture staples and yields all
    eight capture-face helices without changing the accepted cadnano JSON.
zh_CN.Trace a closed specimen/background envel:
Trace a closed specimen/background envelope from the raw TEM.

    A specimen outline and an internal crystallographic boundary are not the
    same segmentation problem.  The former is normally a single, large,
    centre-containing envelope.  Searching a continuous radius around the
    full 360 degrees prevents a coarse local-FFT mask from folding back onto
    internal Moire cells or producing self-intersecting loops.  A three-turn
    Viterbi pass enforces angular continuity while still retaining corners and
    curved physical edges.

    Full-field specimens have no image-visible exterior.  They are rejected
    by the normalized-radius gate and therefore do not acquire an artificial
    green contour (the ``twin2.tif`` regression case).

zh_CN.Find an open sample/background edge from:
Find an open sample/background edge from local FFT periodicity.

    The radial specimen detector is intentionally conservative and only
    accepts a centre-containing closed envelope.  Real TEM crops frequently
    contain a crystalline sheet that continues through two or three image
    edges, leaving only one open specimen/background interface.  In that
    geometry a closed radial contour is impossible.

    This fallback performs a Photoshop-magic-wand-like classification on a
    coarse grid after local background flattening: crystalline sample tiles
    have concentrated reciprocal-space peaks, whereas amorphous support or
    empty background has a diffuse FFT.  It is enabled only when the two
    periodicity classes are strongly separated.  Full-field twins and ordinary
    orientation domains therefore remain domains rather than being mislabeled
    as sample/background.

NumPy-only TEM/FFT analyzer executed outside the Qt process.

    A compact bilateral filter keeps the core NumPy-only.  The range scale is
    estimated from the image itself, so it smooths TEM/SEM shot noise without
    averaging a bright particle edge into its background.

DNA Moiré Designer prototype

    ``lattice_constant_nm`` is the Square nearest-neighbour spacing and the

    nearest neighbours are therefore separated by half that value.

Deterministic staged structure generation for the Square moire seed.

The public functions in this module deliberately keep caDNAno model imports

then this module validates the legacy JSON before the UI exposes it.

    A representative particle is strongest evidence.  Otherwise compare the

    This intentionally describes image signal, not AFM physical height.
en.Central, offline localization for the Mo:
Central, offline localization for the Moiré Designer UI and exports.

The application historically contained literal Chinese/English UI strings.
This module deliberately translates at the presentation boundary so existing
design algorithms and serialized scientific identifiers stay unchanged.
en.Run the existing orthogonal-sequence des:
Run the existing orthogonal-sequence designer inside DNA Moiré Designer.

The parameter dialog and generation/export flow intentionally mirror the
existing implementation.  This module owns the launch path so opening the
tool never requires a cadnano document controller or cadnano main window.
en.Use one arithmetic-mean frame size per r:
Use one arithmetic-mean frame size per reference role and shape.

    Each exemplar keeps its own image texture and angle.  Only the search-frame
    width/height are standardized, so a slightly loose or tight automatic fit
    does not propagate as a separate particle size throughout the image.
en.Build a calibrated prediction for the se:
Build a calibrated prediction for the selected bilayer and Square Seed.

    Nominal Z lengths remain independent design inputs.  Angle/period solves
    the distributed mean indel, which changes the mean physical Z2/spacing
    length while leaving its shared SST/Seed crossover coordinates intact.
en.Use one color for both 16-bp halves of e:
Use one color for both 16-bp halves of every 32-bp pair.

    Physical A0/B0 staples and the normal staples occupying the legal A1/B1
    extension targets use the same pair color.  Thus each layer has one color
    per 32-bp capture pair even before translated capture sequences are
    materialized during export.
en.Locate repeated TEM units near an FFT-pr:
Locate repeated TEM units near an FFT-predicted period.

    A normalized template correlation supplies candidate unit centres. The
    final period is the median of neighbour distances along two approximately
    orthogonal axes, so the FFT prediction constrains the search without
    forcing the TEM measurement to equal it.
en.Return complete 16-bp domain bounds arou:
Return complete 16-bp domain bounds around each duplex layer.

    The five validated 96/104/112/120/128-bp examples alternate which
    polymer owns the eight-base outer overhang.  Repeating that boundary
    state every 32 bp makes lengthening the exact inverse of shortening:
    only complete 32-nt U strands are added or removed.
en.Methods mixed into ``MoireDesignerWindow:
Methods mixed into ``MoireDesignerWindow``.

    All raster exports use the exact TEM source width and height and SVG view
    boxes use those same dimensions.  Embedded FFTs additionally use isotropic
    reciprocal-space axes, so a rectangular TEM cannot stretch FFT angles or
    turn a Square first-order peak set into a rectangle.
en.Nick target-bearing staples at legal lon:
Nick target-bearing staples at legal longitudinal positions.

    A connected physical staple already includes its 16-nt capture segment,
    so 64 nt is an absolute limit and 57 nt is preferred.  A normal staple
    on a translated/export-only target must leave room for that future
    segment: its corresponding limits are therefore 48 and 41 nt.
en.Straighten an isolated short product int:
Straighten an isolated short product into adjacent normal staples.

    This is the final edge-case repair for variable 8-bp endpoints.  It acts
    only on a non-capture component: internal crossovers of that short product
    are opened, each contiguous helix run is joined to a neighboring normal
    staple, and no Seed–SST edge is ever changed.
en.Seal boundary nicks until every non-capt:
Seal boundary nicks until every non-capture staple is synthesizable.

    Reference capture windows and automatically generated Seed routing meet
    at deterministic same-helix boundaries.  Sealing only an adjacent pair of
    open 5'/3' records preserves all crossover sites while avoiding small
    products caused solely by the former window crop.
en.Rotate a lattice graph and remove the co:
Rotate a lattice graph and remove the complete central Seed footprint.

    The exclusion square stays aligned with the Square Seed, matching the 2-D
    preview where both SST layers are drawn first and the full 8 x 8 Seed area
    is then cleared.  Edges touching a removed helix are removed as well, so
    no SST bond enters the reserved Seed area.
en.Build two permanent left/right Seed scaf:
Build two permanent left/right Seed scaffold molecules.

    This is deliberately a Moiré-only generator.  It reuses the validated
    Seed-S topology, preserves the balanced 10/11-bp outer edge adjustment,
    and joins complete secondary 32-bp modules with explicit seams.  It does
    not alter or configure cadnano's normal AutoCS_scaffolds command.
en.Return SST, Seed-support and maximum-den:
Return SST, Seed-support and maximum-density capture ranges.

    ``z1_bp``/``z3_bp`` remain the SST lengths for compatibility with staged
    files.  Seed targets are separate, single-base inputs.  Full coverage
    reserves three bases here; legal per-helix crossover endpoints and seams
    are realized by the routing worker without global 8-bp snapping.
en.Remove only crossover blocks required to:
Remove only crossover blocks required to reunite dense loops.

    Adding all 1/32 candidates creates several legal closed loops.  Restoring
    a longitudinal block whose two crossover halves lie in different loops
    merges exactly those loops.  Repeating this operation produces one loop
    while retaining the maximum possible number of dense legal crossovers.
en.Return the Seed support target passed to:
Return the Seed support target passed to legal crossover routing.

    Seed input is intentionally single-base.  Endpoint legality is handled by
    the per-helix 10/11-bp edge redistribution and seam merger in the routing
    worker, so this stage must not round the whole support zone to 8 bp.
    Requested full coverage still reserves at least three bases beyond SST.
en.Translate a validated left/right routing:
Translate a validated left/right routing into balanced band bounds.

    Internal reciprocal crossover blocks keep their reference topology.
    The low edge is used as the translation anchor.  Endpoint crossovers are
    moved to the requested legal outer boundary, while crossover blocks that
    fall outside a shortened band are healed into ordinary longitudinal DNA.
en.Resolve the two first-order Square Bragg:
Resolve the two first-order Square Bragg families from a TEM image.

    Median/mean patch spectra suppress the specimen envelope and the much
    lower-frequency moire modulation.  The closest-to-centre rule is applied
    only after sharp peaks have formed two reciprocal, orthogonal Square
    families; central background and moire satellites are therefore not
    eligible lattice peaks.
en.Frozen Square missing-helix calibration:
Frozen Square missing-helix calibration used by design prediction.

The nodes are the finalized 2026-08-02 SNUPI matrix.  Each profile is
``(x0, T0, k_minus, k_plus)`` and each descriptor contains missing fraction,
eccentricity, polar-moment ratio, boundary fraction, mean neighbour degree
and mean wall depth.  This copy keeps DNA Moiré Designer independent from a
particular cadnano installation.
en.Build an in-memory A1/B1 alternative use:
Build an in-memory A1/B1 alternative used only for sequence export.

    The accepted design remains A0/B0 and therefore connects only Seed
    helices 16–19 and 47–44 in public SST-first numbering.  This derived copy
    swaps those bridges for their 4x4-unit translations, allowing cadnano's
    sequence engine to calculate the other four helices on each face without
    adding those bridges to the accepted structure JSON.
en.Build one legal closed Seed band from tr:
Build one legal closed Seed band from translated native endpoints.

    Square scaffold endpoint phases repeat every 32 bases.  The validated
    Seed-S reference supplies complementary low/high endpoint matchings; a
    whole-period translation therefore remains a native crossover.  Keeping
    only those endpoint rings and then adding legal seams avoids translating
    hundreds of interior crossovers by helix-specific offsets.
en.Absolute lattice orientations for a TEM-:
Absolute lattice orientations for a TEM-registered reconstruction.

        FFT orientations are mathematical angles (positive y points upward).
        The returned values retain that convention; drawing code converts them
        to image coordinates.  When TEM real-space period supplies a refined
        relative twist, preserve the FFT-measured absolute mean orientation and
        distribute that refined twist symmetrically around the mean.
en.Absorb sub-32-bp crop remnants without d:
Absorb sub-32-bp crop remnants without deleting scaffold bases.

    Moving an old closure inward can leave a 20-bp terminal loop bounded by
    the old reciprocal crossover block.  It is not a complete 32-bp module
    and therefore must not receive a seam.  Removing that one crossover block
    restores both longitudinal bonds and absorbs the bases into the adjacent
    main loop.  Complete 32/64-bp modules are intentionally left for the
    explicit seam merger below.
en.Return geometry and text scales for anno:
Return geometry and text scales for annotations on Uploaded TEM.

        Geometry remains resolution-aware so boxes, markers and line weights
        keep their relative placement on the exported original-resolution
        image.  Font point sizes deliberately do *not* scale with raster pixel
        count: a cryo/high-resolution upload must use the same annotation type
        size as an ordinary TEM rather than treating extra pixels as a reason
        to enlarge its text.
en.Fit an FFT without distorting reciprocal:
Fit an FFT without distorting reciprocal-space geometry.

        A rectangular TEM produces a rectangular FFT array, but one FFT pixel
        represents ``1 / image_width`` in x and ``1 / image_height`` in y.
        Treating those array pixels as equal-sized display pixels therefore
        stretches angles and a Square reciprocal lattice.  Fit by the
        *normalised frequency span* instead: the complete FFT is square and a
        fractional centre crop keeps the same physical x/y scale.  This is the
        native, undistorted reciprocal-space aspect used by the on-screen
        preview and by both PNG and SVG exports.
en.Materialize both 4x4 SST translations ar:
Materialize both 4x4 SST translations around the accepted 8x8 Seed.

    The accepted cadnano file intentionally contains only the origin A0/B0
    capture bridges.  Sequence export derives the A1/B1 translation in
    memory.  For the assembled atomistic model we need both physical copies:
    retain the accepted SST unit, duplicate the translated unit four lattice
    columns to its right, and apply the translated capture routing only to
    the second four helices on each Seed face.  The two face groups are
    disjoint, so this preserves the origin capture staples and yields all
    eight capture-face helices without changing the accepted cadnano JSON.

en.Rasterize a vector polygon only for stab:
Rasterize a vector polygon only for stable area integration.

    Rendering remains fully vectorial.  This bounded-resolution mask is used
    solely to normalize domain percentages inside an arbitrary curved sample
    boundary without requiring an optional geometry package.
en.Close one measured open seam along both:
Close one measured open seam along both possible frame routes.

    This makes the numerical area and translucent overlay use the same
    precise TEM-refined boundary, rather than the earlier local-FFT cell
    staircase.  More complex multi-domain topologies retain the conservative
    cell-based fallback.
en.Estimate the short lattice spacing direc:
Estimate the short lattice spacing directly from TEM autocorrelation.

    This is deliberately independent of the reciprocal-space distance used
    for the FFT value reported in the bulk CSV.  The FFT estimate is only used
    to define a broad, physically plausible annulus; the final distance comes
    from real-space correlation peaks.
en.Detect visible reciprocal peaks and pres:
Detect visible reciprocal peaks and preserve their complex phase.

    The detector uses the real FFT of the uploaded TEM, sub-pixel peak
    centroids, compact locally fitted ellipses, and exact Friedel partners.
    Raw arrays keep the source width:height ratio.  The GUI displays them on
    isotropic reciprocal-space axes, so FFT geometry is not stretched.
en.Extend only near-frame open endpoints to:
Extend only near-frame open endpoints to the image boundary.

    Local FFT windows cannot be centred closer than half a patch to an image
    edge.  Consequently, a real domain seam that exits the image is otherwise
    drawn with two short missing end pieces.  This function adds those pieces
    before TEM evidence refinement.  Closed/internal contours are untouched.
en.Find an optional pore/supercell lattice:
Find an optional pore/supercell lattice sharing the helix orientation.

    A valid pore lattice must provide Friedel pairs along both axes of the
    already established single-layer Square helix lattice.  Its spacing must
    be a near-integer multiple of the helix spacing; this rejects arbitrary
    low-frequency texture, contamination and unrelated domain envelopes.
en.Combine specimen contrast with the prove:
Combine specimen contrast with the proven domain-seam evidence.

    Sample/background classification and domain classification remain
    independent.  Only the final sub-pixel/vector placement is shared: broad
    mass-thickness contrast keeps the path on the specimen rim, while the
    texture-orientation and dark-ridge terms make it hug the visible TEM edge
    as accurately as a domain/domain boundary.
en.Return real-space evidence specialized f:
Return real-space evidence specialized for specimen/background edges.

    Domain seams are dominated by lattice-orientation changes, whereas a
    specimen outline is usually expressed by a broad mass-thickness/tone edge
    plus a change in periodic texture.  Keeping these evidence maps separate
    prevents the sample contour from snapping to a strong internal lattice
    transition, as happened in high-resolution cryo/TEM fields.
en.Trace a mostly vertical/horizontal seam:
Trace a mostly vertical/horizontal seam at near-pixel resolution.

    A coarse local-FFT boundary is a staircase of cell edges.  Offsetting
    nodes only along each edge normal cannot turn that staircase into the
    oblique physical seam.  When the observed boundary is predominantly
    monotone, use every TEM row (or column) as a free path state and solve a
    continuity-regularized dynamic program through the dark-seam evidence.
en.Return multi-scale TEM evidence for a vi:
Return multi-scale TEM evidence for a visible grain/domain boundary.

    Local FFT determines which lattice family lies on each side.  The visible
    seam itself is positioned from the TEM: slow intensity edges, changes in
    local texture orientation/anisotropy, variance transitions and dark grain
    boundary ridges.  The calculation is deliberately performed at a bounded
    resolution and never invents a spline-smoothed boundary.
en.Remove local-FFT grid staircases while r:
Remove local-FFT grid staircases while retaining measured bends.

    TEM domain contours arrive as connected vector segments.  Douglas-Peucker
    reduction is applied independently to each open chain, followed by two
    conservative corner-cut passes.  The tolerance is tied to the local-FFT
    stride/search scale, so a visible large bend survives while dozens of
    horizontal/vertical micro-steps become one oblique or gently curved run.
en.Return TEM evidence centred on a visibly:
Return TEM evidence centred on a visibly dark twin/grain seam.

    An orientation-gradient map has two maxima, one on either shoulder of a
    dark physical seam.  Snapping to that map alone can therefore draw a line
    parallel to, but several pixels away from, the boundary.  For same-a,
    same-symmetry twins we combine the texture evidence with a dark
    difference-of-Gaussians ridge so the reported vector follows the seam
    centre rather than a local-FFT cell centre or one of its shoulders.
en.Map validated lattice families to their:
Map validated lattice families to their real-space domains.

    The historical name is retained for compatibility.  A family may contain
    the two reciprocal axes of a Square lattice or the three reciprocal axes
    of a sixfold lattice.  Global FFT establishes the allowed bases;
    overlapping local FFTs then assign symmetry, spacing and orientation to
    each spatial domain.  Connected components and boundaries are emitted in
    source-image coordinates for identical raster/SVG rendering by the GUI.
en.Return clear peaks belonging to validate:
Return clear peaks belonging to validated reciprocal bases.

    Every accepted Friedel pair must be expressible as

        G(h,k) = h*g1 + k*g2,  h,k integers.

    For Square this includes the familiar 45-degree (h,h)/(h,-h) diagonal
    shell.  Honeycomb/Kagome/hexagonal families use their measured oblique
    reciprocal basis, so their legal higher-order angles emerge from integer
    indices rather than from a hard-coded 45-degree rule.  Missing or weak
    theoretical reflections are never synthesized.
en.Build Square and sixfold lattice hypothe:
Build Square and sixfold lattice hypotheses from measured FFT peaks.

    Each hypothesis is an actual Friedel-paired set of reciprocal peaks.  The
    local-domain stage decides where it is present; no symmetry is inferred
    from a single line or from an unpaired maximum.  Honeycomb is reserved for
    a near-60/60/60 first-order family.  The user-supplied cryo-EM Kagome
    reference is represented by the experimentally distorted sixfold family,
    typically containing one 65--70 degree reciprocal-axis gap.  Ambiguous
    sixfold families remain explicitly ``Hexagonal``.
en.Trace a closed specimen/background envel:
Trace a closed specimen/background envelope from the raw TEM.

    A specimen outline and an internal crystallographic boundary are not the
    same segmentation problem.  The former is normally a single, large,
    centre-containing envelope.  Searching a continuous radius around the
    full 360 degrees prevents a coarse local-FFT mask from folding back onto
    internal Moire cells or producing self-intersecting loops.  A three-turn
    Viterbi pass enforces angular continuity while still retaining corners and
    curved physical edges.

    Full-field specimens have no image-visible exterior.  They are rejected
    by the normalized-radius gate and therefore do not acquire an artificial
    green contour (the ``twin2.tif`` regression case).
en.Find an open sample/background edge from:
Find an open sample/background edge from local FFT periodicity.

    The radial specimen detector is intentionally conservative and only
    accepts a centre-containing closed envelope.  Real TEM crops frequently
    contain a crystalline sheet that continues through two or three image
    edges, leaving only one open specimen/background interface.  In that
    geometry a closed radial contour is impossible.

    This fallback performs a Photoshop-magic-wand-like classification on a
    coarse grid after local background flattening: crystalline sample tiles
    have concentrated reciprocal-space peaks, whereas amorphous support or
    empty background has a diffuse FFT.  It is enabled only when the two
    periodicity classes are strongly separated.  Full-field twins and ordinary
    orientation domains therefore remain domains rather than being mislabeled
    as sample/background.
